svg.title: Oneirodex glyph
svg.desc: Silhouette of the Oneirodex mark — a closed cabinet (lintel, uprights, shelf) holding a shelf of game cases, solid on transparent, with no plate behind it. The lintel is what makes this a theca (a case), not a U-shape that can be read as a controller body. This exists so the mark can be *themed*. oneirodex_mark.svg bakes the default green (#12a4a0 -> #4ef2a1) and a #0b0d10 plate into the file, and an external SVG loaded through an element cannot see the page's custom properties, so on any preset other than the default the brand stayed green while everything around it changed. A monochrome silhouette can be used as a CSS mask-image and painted with var(--od-accent), which reaches an arbitrary theme colour exactly — where filter: hue-rotate() only approximates one and collapses on the near-greyscale presets. Keep the geometry in step with oneirodex_mark.svg: same viewBox, same coordinates. Only the fills differ, and only because a mask reads alpha. Angle brackets in this text are escaped, and must stay escaped. An SVG is XML: a bare tag written in prose here opens an element that is never closed, the whole document fails to parse, and a mask whose source will not decode paints nothing at all — the element keeps its box and the mark silently disappears. That is exactly how the brand went missing from the rail, and nothing caught it because every check asked whether the file was *served*. tests/test_static_svg.py parses it now.
